questions.question: Media ensures government accountability through: a). Censorship b). Investigative journalism c). Elections d). Imprisonment
questions.solution_html:
• Spying
  • • Spying, or espionage, refers to the covert gathering of confidential, classified, or sensitive information

questions.question: Law commissions recommended that media must balance right to free speech with right to a). Privacy b). Equality c). Free Assembly d). Free Movement
questions.solution_html:
• Article 19(1)(a) and Restrictions on Reporting Criminal Investigations
  • • Article 19(1)(a) guarantees freedom of speech and expression, including press freedom, but Article 19(2)
  • permits reasonable restrictions in the interests of public order, decency, and justice
  • • Reporting on ongoing criminal investigations can prejudice fair trials, influence witnesses, and compromise
  • the accused's right to a fair hearing — justifying restrictions on media coverage
  • • The balance requires that restrictions be proportionate, legally sanctioned, and not used to suppress
  • legitimate public interest journalism under the guise of protecting investigations
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: legitimate public interest journalism under the guise of protecting investigations

questions.question: Restrictions must be: a).Unreasonable b). Strictly unlimited c). Reasonable d). Permanent
questions.solution_html:
• Shreya Singhal v. Union of India and Media Freedom
  • • In this landmark 2015 judgment, the Supreme Court struck down Section 66A of the Information Technology
  • Act, which penalised online speech found to be "offensive" or "menacing" — terms too vague to constitute
  • reasonable restrictions under Article 19(2)
  • • The judgment significantly expanded digital media freedom by holding that the state cannot curtail online
  • expression arbitrarily and that restrictions must meet the specific grounds listed in Article 19(2)
  • • It established that the chilling effect of vague internet speech laws on legitimate journalism, activism, and
  • public discourse is constitutionally impermissible, making it a foundational precedent for digital rights.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: public discourse is constitutionally impermissible, making it a foundational precedent for digital rights.

questions.question: Criminal contempt includes: a). Non-payment of rent b). Scandalizing court c). Filing case d). Voting
questions.solution_html:
• Scope of Freedom of Speech and Expression

questions.question: Utterances that threaten authority of the state is punishable under a). Copy Right b). Contempt of Court c). Sedition d). Defamation
questions.solution_html:
• Freedom of Press vs. Defamation, Sedition, and National Security
  • • Defamation — Section 499 and 500 of the IPC criminalise defamation, creating tension with press freedom;
  • the Subramanian Swamy v. Union of India (2016) case upheld criminal defamation's constitutionality, though
  • press freedom advocates argue it has a chilling effect on investigative journalism
  • • Sedition — Section 124A IPC punishes speech that excites disaffection against the government; historically
  • misused against journalists and activists, the Supreme Court in Kedar Nath Singh v. State of Bihar (1962)
  • limited its scope to speech inciting actual violence, yet its misuse persists in cases like Vinod Dua v. Union of
  • India (2021)
  • • National security — the Official Secrets Act and UAPA create significant barriers to reporting on security
  • matters, often conflicting with the public's right to know about state conduct
  • • The tension is fundamentally about where the line falls between speech that serves democratic
  • accountability and speech that genuinely threatens individuals or the state
  • • Courts have consistently held that restrictions must be narrowly tailored, proportionate, and not used as
  • instruments of political suppression — a standard that remains contested in practice
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: instruments of political suppression — a standard that remains contested in practice

questions.question: Explain the objectives of Justice mentioned in the Preamble.
questions.solution_html:
• Objectives of Justice in the Preamble
  • • The Preamble to the Indian Constitution commits to securing social, economic, and political justice for all
  • citizens
  • • Social justice ensures equal treatment regardless of caste, religion, gender, or class; economic justice aims at
  • equitable distribution of resources and opportunities
  • • Political justice guarantees equal political rights and participation, ensuring that every citizen has an equal
  • voice in democratic governance
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: voice in democratic governance

questions.question: Why are legislative privileges important in a democracy?
questions.solution_html:
• Importance of Legislative Privileges in a Democracy
  • • Legislative privileges protect members of Parliament and State Legislatures from legal proceedings for
  • anything said or done in the course of legislative proceedings, ensuring free and fearless debate
  • • They safeguard the independence of the legislature from interference by the executive or judiciary
  • preserving the separation of powers
  • • For media, legislative privilege means reports of parliamentary proceedings published in good faith are
  • protected from defamation suits, enabling transparent public reporting of governance
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: protected from defamation suits, enabling transparent public reporting of governance

questions.question: What are the powers and functions of the Supreme Court of India?
questions.solution_html:
• Powers and Functions of the Supreme Court of India
  • • The Supreme Court exercises original jurisdiction in disputes between states or between states and the
  • Union, and appellate jurisdiction over High Court decisions in civil, criminal, and constitutional matters
  • • It is the final interpreter of the Constitution and has the power of judicial review to strike down laws
  • inconsistent with constitutional provisions
  • • The Supreme Court also has advisory jurisdiction under Article 143, allowing the President to seek its opinion
  • on questions of law or fact of public importance
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: on questions of law or fact of public importance

questions.question: What is meant by censorship in the media?
questions.solution_html:
• Censorship in Media
  • • Censorship is the suppression, restriction, or regulation of content in media — print, broadcast, film, or
  • digital — by a government authority, institution, or other controlling body before or after publication
  • • Pre-censorship (prior restraint) prevents publication of content deemed harmful, while post-publication
  • censorship involves removal or ban of already published material
  • • In India, the Constitution permits reasonable censorship of films (through the Central Board of Film
  • Certification) and wartime media restrictions, but prior restraint on the press is generally not permissible
  • under constitutional jurisprudence
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: under constitutional jurisprudence

questions.question: What are the consequences of irresponsible journalism?
questions.solution_html:
• Consequences of Irresponsible Journalism
  • • Irresponsible journalism can cause irreparable reputational harm to individuals through inaccurate
  • sensationalised, or defamatory reporting, exposing media organisations to legal liability
  • • It erodes public trust in the media institution as a whole, undermining the press's democratic role as a
  • credible Fourth Estate
  • • In extreme cases, irresponsible reporting — particularly during communal tensions or crises — can incite
  • public disorder, violence, and panic, making it a matter of both ethical and legal consequence
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: public disorder, violence, and panic, making it a matter of both ethical and legal consequence

questions.question: Discuss the role of the Information Technology Act in regulating content published on digital media platforms
questions.solution_html:
• Role of the Information Technology Act in Regulating Digital Media
  • • The Information Technology Act, 2000 (amended 2008) provides the primary legislative framework for
  • regulating content on digital platforms, covering cybercrimes, data protection, and intermediary liability
  • • Section 79 grants safe harbour protection to intermediaries who act as passive conduits, provided they
  • comply with government takedown notices and due diligence requirements
  • • The IT (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021 further regulate online news
  • portals and OTT platforms, requiring grievance redressal mechanisms and content classification
  • significantly expanding state oversight of digital journalism
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: significantly expanding state oversight of digital journalism

questions.question: Discuss the sources, functions, and importance of law in maintaining social order.
questions.solution_html:
• Sources, Functions, and Importance of Law in Maintaining Social Order
  • • Sources of law include legislation (statutes enacted by Parliament and State Legislatures), judicial precedents
  • (case law established by courts), customary law, constitutional provisions, and personal laws governing
  • specific communities
  • • Regulatory function — law defines acceptable conduct, establishes rights and duties, and provides
  • mechanisms for resolving disputes between individuals and the state
  • • Protective function — law safeguards fundamental rights, protects the vulnerable from exploitation, and
  • ensures equality before the law regardless of social position
  • • Social change function — law acts as an instrument of social reform, as seen in legislation abolishing
  • untouchability, ensuring women's rights, and regulating child labour
  • • Importance for media — a robust legal framework protects press freedom while holding journalists
  • accountable, balancing the democratic necessity of free expression with the equally important need for
  • social order and individual dignity
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: social order and individual dignity

questions.question: Explain the meaning, nature, and differences between Civil Law and Criminal Law.
questions.solution_html:
• Civil Law vs. Criminal Law — Meaning, Nature, and Differences
  • • Civil law governs disputes between private parties — individuals, organisations — concerning rights, property
  • contracts, and torts; the objective is to provide remedy (compensation or injunction) to the aggrieved party
  • rather than to punish
  • • Criminal law deals with offences against society at large; the state prosecutes the accused and the objective
  • is punishment — imprisonment, fine, or both — to deter future offences and maintain public order
  • • Standard of proof differs fundamentally: civil cases require proof on the balance of probabilities, while
  • criminal cases demand proof beyond reasonable doubt — a significantly higher threshold
  • • Parties and procedure: civil suits are filed by the aggrieved party (plaintiff vs. defendant); criminal cases are
  • prosecuted by the state (prosecution vs. accused) through the police and public prosecutor
  • • Media relevance: defamation can be both civil (suit for damages) and criminal (prosecution under IPC);
  • contempt of court, copyright infringement, and privacy violations may attract civil liability, while sedition
  • obscenity, and cybercrimes attract criminal prosecution
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: obscenity, and cybercrimes attract criminal prosecution

questions.question: Analyse the objectives of Copy Right Law in digital media age
questions.solution_html:
• Objectives of Copyright Law in the Digital Media Age
  • • Protection of creative rights — copyright law grants authors, journalists, photographers, and content creators
  • exclusive rights over their original works, preventing unauthorised reproduction, distribution, and
  • commercial exploitation
  • • Incentivising creation — by guaranteeing economic returns through licensing, royalties, and moral rights
  • copyright law encourages continued investment in original content creation in digital environments
  • • Addressing digital challenges — the digital age has made copying, sharing, and remixing content
  • instantaneous and global, requiring copyright law to evolve through the Digital Millennium Copyright Act (US)
  • and India's IT Act amendments to address online piracy, fair use in digital contexts, and platform liability
  • • Balancing public interest — fair use/fair dealing provisions allow limited use of copyrighted material for
  • education, research, criticism, and news reporting — preserving the press's ability to quote and analyse
  • content without infringing copyright
  • • Platform accountability — in the digital age, copyright law increasingly focuses on the responsibility of platforms
  • (YouTube, social media) to prevent infringement through content ID systems and takedown mechanisms, raising
  • critical questions about the balance between creator rights, platform freedom, and public access to information
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: critical questions about the balance between creator rights, platform freedom, and public access to information
